1:
\textbf{(a)} Clovis: $(t,C)=(1,16)$ and $(5,19)$, slope $\frac{3}{4}$:
\[C(t)=16+\tfrac34(t-1)=15.25+0.75t.\]
\textbf{(b)} Isobel: $(0,68)$ and $(6,75)$, slope $\frac76$:
\[I(t)=68+\tfrac76 t.\]
\textbf{(c)} Solve $I=3C$: $68+\frac76t=45.75+2.25t\Rightarrow 22.25=\big(2.25-\tfrac76\big)t\Rightarrow t\approx20.54$.
So Isobel earns three times as much as Clovis about 20.5 years after 2001, i.e. \boxed{\text{in 2021}} (mid-2021).
2:
\textbf{(a)} $y=Ab^t$ with $A=15$ (the 1982 amount). In 2007 ($t=25$): $15b^{25}=8$, so
\[b=\Big(\frac{8}{15}\Big)^{1/25}\approx0.97517,\qquad y=15(0.97517)^t.\]
\textbf{(b)} 1996 is $t=14$: $y=15(0.97517)^{14}\approx\boxed{10.55\ \text{grams}}$.

\textbf{(c)} $15b^t=2\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{\ln(2/15)}{\ln b}\approx80.13$, so \boxed{\text{in 2062}} (early 2062).
3:
A linear-to-linear function: $S(t)=\dfrac{at+b}{ct+1}$ with $S(0)=4$, $S(3)=10$, $S(6)=22$.

$S(0)=4\Rightarrow b=4$. $S(3)=10\Rightarrow 3a+4=10(3c+1)\Rightarrow a=10c+2$. $S(6)=22\Rightarrow 6a+4=22(6c+1)$, so $60c+16=132c+22\Rightarrow c=-\tfrac1{12}$, $a=\tfrac76$:
\[S(t)=\frac{\frac76t+4}{1-\frac{t}{12}}=\frac{14t+48}{12-t}.\]
(Check: $S(3)=90/9=10$, $S(6)=132/6=22$.) Set $S(t)=202$: $14t+48=2424-202t\Rightarrow 216t=2376\Rightarrow t=11$.

\textbf{Answer:} on their \boxed{11\text{th anniversary}} (11 years after marrying).
4:
\textbf{(a)} Juliet goes from $(10,20)$ to the origin in 5 s:
\[x_J=10-2t,\qquad y_J=20-4t.\]
\textbf{(b)} Romeo goes from $(30,0)$ to the origin in 2 s:
\[x_R=30-15t,\qquad y_R=0.\]
\textbf{(c)} Squared distance:
\[D(t)=(x_J-x_R)^2+(y_J-y_R)^2=(13t-20)^2+(20-4t)^2=185t^2-680t+800.\]
This quadratic is smallest at $t=\dfrac{680}{2\cdot185}=\dfrac{68}{37}\approx\boxed{1.84\ \text{s}}$ (they are then about 13.2 m apart).
5:
Place the start at the origin with East $=+x$, North $=+y$.
\begin{itemize}
\item $0\le t\le3$: position $(2t,0)$, distance $2t$.
\item $3\le t\le4$: she is at $(6,0)$ then walks north: $(6,\,3(t-3))$.
\item $4\le t\le8$: from $(6,3)$ east at 5 km/h: $(6+5(t-4),\,3)=(5t-14,\,3)$.
\end{itemize}
\[d(t)=\begin{cases}2t, & 0\le t\le3\\ \sqrt{36+9(t-3)^2}, & 3< t\le4\\ \sqrt{(5t-14)^2+9}, & 4< t\le8\end{cases}\quad\text{(km, $t$ in hours)}\]
6:
The ground is the line $y=5x$ (it rises 5 ft per horizontal foot from the bottom of the hill at the origin).

\textbf{(a)} Landing: $-5x^2+36x=5x\Rightarrow x(31-5x)=0\Rightarrow x=6.2$. The balloon lands at \boxed{(6.2,\ 31)}.

\textbf{(b)} Height above the ground (vertical distance) is
\[h(x)=(-5x^2+36x)-5x=-5x^2+31x,\]
maximized at $x=\frac{31}{10}=3.1$: $h(3.1)=-5(9.61)+96.1=\boxed{48.05\ \text{ft}}$.
7:
Max 112 at $t=2$, next min 88 at $t=7$: half-period 5, period 10, midline 100, amplitude 12:
\[L(t)=100+12\cos\!\Big(\frac{2\pi}{10}(t-2)\Big).\]
$L>94\iff\cos\!\big(\frac{\pi}{5}(t-2)\big)>-\frac12\iff \frac{\pi}{5}(t-2)\in\big(-\tfrac{2\pi}{3}+2\pi k,\ \tfrac{2\pi}{3}+2\pi k\big)$,
i.e. $t\in\big(2-\tfrac{10}{3}+10k,\ 2+\tfrac{10}{3}+10k\big)$. In $[0,13]$ that is
\[[0,\,5.333)\quad\text{and}\quad(8.667,\,13].\]
Total: $5.333+4.333\approx\boxed{9.67\ \text{seconds}}$.
8:
\textbf{(a)} In 3 min $=180$ s the horse runs $3600$ ft, an angle of $\frac{3600}{100}=36$ rad clockwise. Starting angle is $-\frac{\pi}{2}$ (the point $(0,-100)$), so the final angle is $\theta=-\frac{\pi}{2}-36$:
\[(100\cos\theta,\ 100\sin\theta)\approx\boxed{(99.18,\ 12.80)}.\]
\textbf{(b)} The line through $(100,0)$ with $y$-intercept 50 is $y=50-\frac{x}{2}$. Intersect with $x^2+y^2=10000$:
\[x^2+\Big(50-\frac x2\Big)^2=10000\Rightarrow \tfrac54x^2-50x-7500=0\Rightarrow x^2-40x-6000=0,\]
so $x=100$ (start) or $x=-60$, giving the far point $(-60,80)$. Distance: $\sqrt{160^2+80^2}=\sqrt{32000}\approx178.9$ ft. Time at 40 ft/s: $\dfrac{178.9}{40}\approx\boxed{4.47\ \text{s}}$.
9:
From the graph, $f$ is an arch on $[-1,1]$ with $f(\pm1)=0$ and maximum $f(0)=3$; its range is $[0,3]$.

\textbf{(a)} $g(x)=-\frac13f(2x)$: squeeze horizontally by a factor of 2, then flip over the $x$-axis and scale vertically by $\frac13$. The graph of $g$ is an upside-down arch through $(-\frac12,0)$, down to its minimum $(0,-1)$, and back up to $(\frac12,0)$.

\textbf{(b)} Domain: need $-1\le2x\le1$, so \boxed{-\tfrac12\le x\le\tfrac12}.

\textbf{(c)} Range: $f(2x)\in[0,3]$, so $g\in$ \boxed{[-1,\,0]}.

\textbf{(d)} One choice: restrict $f$ to $[0,1]$, where it decreases from $f(0)=3$ to $f(1)=0$ (so it is one-to-one). Its inverse $f^{-1}$ has domain $[0,3]$ and range $[0,1]$; its graph is the reflection of that piece across the line $y=x$, running from $(0,1)$ down to $(3,0)$. (Restricting to $[-1,0]$ also works.)
